trust_decision.summary: Whether a caller-supplied name/uri can terminate the generated string literal and inject code is decided independently in three places: stringifyUnicodeSafe's unicode branch (the shared low-level stringifier, which also gates every value printed into a generated .sol via printValue), the Foundry test interpolation, and the Hardhat test interpolation. The two zip test generators do not call the stringifier at all, and the stringifier itself escapes only a double quote in its unicode branch, so a backslash still breaks out.

landing_point.why: The advisory names generated Foundry and Hardhat tests; getContractSpecificTestFunction is the only place in the Foundry packager that puts opts.name/opts.uri inside a quoted literal, and it is mirrored by the single Hardhat equivalent at packages/core/solidity/src/zip-hardhat.ts:43-60. These two hunks are also the only grep hits for a raw opts.name/opts.uri interpolation in the tree.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: "printContract already sanitizes the contract file" - a solver who reproduces with a plain double quote sees the unicode branch escape it correctly (and the ASCII branch use JSON.stringify), so the shared stringifier and the generated .sol look safe and out of scope for an advisory about generated test files; only a backslash exposes it.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Non-ASCII names/uris must keep being emitted as Solidity unicode"..." literals (a plain "..." literal cannot carry non-ASCII), while plain-ASCII values must stay byte-identical "..."; and characters with no Solidity escape (NUL, backspace, DEL) plus non-BMP characters must pass through raw. The Hardhat output is TypeScript, so it needs JS escaping, not the Solidity unicode form - the published fix deliberately uses two different escapers (JSON.stringify for the TS test, stringifyUnicodeSafe for the Solidity test/contract). An over-broad fix that escapes non-ASCII as \xNN, drops the unicode"" prefix, or unifies the two escapers breaks legitimate non-ASCII token names/URIs and changes every existing snapshot.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: packages/core/solidity/src/utils/sanitize.test.ts:22-25 and packages/core/solidity/src/utils/sanitize.test.ts:36-40 (unicode"..." output required); packages/core/solidity/src/zip-hardhat.test.ts.md:129 (plain "My Token" must stay unchanged)

O6_input_shapes: plain ASCII name containing a double quote (ERC20/ERC721 name: My "Token")
plain ASCII ERC1155 uri containing a double quote (https://example.com/"id"/{id})
ASCII backslash with no quote (Path\file) - must stay escaped in the ASCII/JSON branch
non-ASCII + backslash + double quote (é\") - the breakout shape in the unicode branch
LF (\n), CR (\r) and vertical tab (0x0B) - line terminators excluded from Solidity's unicode literal body
NUL (0x00), backspace (0x08), DEL (0x7F) - no Solidity escape exists, must pass through raw
non-BMP character (emoji) - must pass through raw, no surrogate escapes
empty string and plain ASCII with no specials - output must stay byte-identical

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Hardhat Ignition module emitting known string constructor arguments inline, e.g. m.contract("MyToken", ["${opts.uri}"])
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The module already emits constructorArgs placeholders for address args (it maps c.constructorArgs at :214), so filling in the string args the wizard already knows is the obvious next feature and would need JSON.stringify - a maintainer could plausibly have written it that way.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Deployment line emitting string constructor arguments as Solidity literals, e.g. instance = new MyToken("${opts.uri}")
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: getDeploymentCode already joins args into the constructor call; today only address variables are passed, but the ERC1155 uri is a constructor value the generator knows, so inlining it is a natural extension and needs the same Solidity escaping.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A neighbouring assertion for another option string, e.g. expect(await instance.symbol()).to.equal("${opts.symbol}")
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: getExpects already asserts name() for ERC20/ERC721; symbol is the adjacent ERC20 option, so a maintainer adding assertion coverage would copy the same interpolation.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A test-file header comment or contract-doc line quoting the token name, e.g. a NatSpec /// @custom:name ${opts.name} in the generated test
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The Foundry test builder composes a header and a contract heading from c values (getHeader at :11-13); adding a human-readable name comment is a plausible documentation improvement and a comment sink needs different escaping from a literal.
